html:
Short answer: pick the system by room size and platform. Small rooms work well with an all-in-one video bar; larger rooms need separate cameras, ceiling or table microphones and room speakers. Remote participants judge a meeting mostly by audio, so microphones matter more than the camera.

By room size

RoomSeatsTypical set-up
Huddle2 to 6Video bar with built-in camera, microphones and speaker, one display
Medium6 to 12Conference camera, table or ceiling microphones, room speakers, one or two displays
Boardroom12 and morePTZ or auto-framing cameras, ceiling microphone arrays with audio processing, dual displays or LED wall, touch control

Teams Rooms, Zoom Rooms or BYOD?

  • Dedicated room system (Teams Rooms or Zoom Rooms): one-touch join from a console, consistent across rooms.
  • Bring your own device: users connect a laptop by USB or wirelessly; flexible for mixed platforms.

Do not forget

  • A stable wired network connection and enough upload bandwidth.
  • Acoustics: echo ruins calls more than anything else.
  • Lighting on faces, not behind people.
  • Training and a support plan.

faqs.q: Which is better, Microsoft Teams Rooms or Zoom Rooms?
faqs.a: Choose the platform your organisation already uses daily. Both support one-touch meetings; many rooms can also join the other platform for external calls.

faqs.q: Why do remote people hear echo from our boardroom?
faqs.a: Usually because of room reflections, poor microphone placement or missing echo cancellation. Proper microphones, audio processing and some acoustic treatment fix it.

faqs.q: Can you standardise all our meeting rooms?
faqs.a: Yes. We create a standard design per room size so every room works the same way, which simplifies support.
